In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
dihydropyrines are able to interact with adenosine A-1 receptors, but this interaction has little or no physiological relevance. (MOL)

dihydropiridines can affect adenosine receptor binding, but not adenosine-mediated signal transduction.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
calcium channel antagonists and agonists affect adenosine receptor binding in vitro and adenosine receptor-mediated functions in vivo.
the calcium channel antagonists verapamil and nifedipin do not affect adenosine binding or function.
the calcium channel antagonists and the calcium channel agonist all have a low affinity for the adenosine receptors and therefore are not useful as adenosine receptor antagonists.
The main takeaway from our work is that
dihydropiridines can affect the A1 receptor.
calcium channel agonists can also act as A1 receptor antagonists and vice versa.
the interaction between adenosine and calcium channels is a complex one.
